prompt:
These ideas were found in different parts of one discussion about: PEP 701 – Syntactic formalization of f-strings
Some are the same idea written differently.

0. Formalize f-string grammar in PEG parser [accepted] - We believe this will be a great improvement in both the maintainability of CPython and the usability of f-strings.; Reduced maintenance costs for f-string parsing code as well us improved usability for users and library developers.
1. Allow comments inside f-string expressions [accepted] - What we are proposing is that this error disappears and anything after the # comment character gets ignored as any comment of any expression (only when the comment is in the expression part).
2. Allow unescaped quotes inside f-string expressions [accepted] - I would like the PEP to note that the existing restrictions on nested quotes (and probably other things) was a deliberate design decision in order to make it easy for editors, syntax highlighters and the like to support f-strings.
3. Allow backslashes inside f-string expressions [accepted] - Thanks for working on this. I look forward to backslashes in expressions!
4. Restrict quote nesting depth for editor support [open] - Another option here is to restrict arbitrary nesting to a specific depth. I think that will allow regex-based lexers to work at the price of having some complex regular expression.
5. Allow arbitrary nesting of quotes in f-string expressions [rejected] - I consider the first two examples terrible code which should be discouraged and the fact that your PEP allows it is a point against it, not in favour.; The biggest problem for me is the reuse of opening quote feature. I get why you want to lift this restriction, and I get that you want to enable arbitrary nesting of quotes, but I think this is helping the machine more than the human.
6. Warn against over-use of same-quote nesting in documentation [accepted] - I voted yes, as I have definitely hit the “you cannot use the same type of quote in the expression part” issue myself. And I think consistency in allowing whatever can be in an expression is easier to explain and understand.; Having said that, I’d prefer it if the PEP warned agains over-use of this feature, as it has the possibility of being difficult to read.
7. Require parentheses around expressions containing same-quote nesting [open] - Rejected ideas, 1: I think you mean wrap in parentheses, as in the example? Would f’{(a !=b)} be an example for ‘!’?
8. Document IDLE limitations regarding quote reuse in f-strings [accepted] - If quote reuse stays, please do so. The SC should know that approving this as is will break a few things. Perhaps add at least “Lexing all possible f-strings with relational expressions will no longer be possible. In particular, reuse of opening quotes in replacement fields will be a problem.”
9. Allow reusing opening quotes inside f-string expressions [accepted] - I voted "no" since for me, the concerns outweigh the benefits in this case. Heavily nested or reused quote characters is a code smell to me.; I think that personal style choices are not a sufficiently strong argument for forbidding quote reuse.
10. Restrict f-string nesting to avoid parser complexity [rejected] - Ignoring the consistency arguments, limiting quote reuse raises quite a lot the complexity. This is because when parsing the expression part now the parser needs to be aware that is parsing an expression inside an f-string with a given quite...; I am not sure what we finally propose (quote reuse or not) as we want to gather some feedback first, but we will discuss this aspect among authors again.
11. Discourage quote reuse via documentation instead of syntax [accepted] - I agree with the people saying that the reuse of quotes in f-strings should not be syntactically incorrect but instead be discouraged in the docs.; At least, I think that personal style choices are not a sufficiently strong argument for forbidding quote reuse.
12. Allow single quotes inside double-quoted f-string expressions [accepted] - I voted Yes because I think that any (unnecessary) restriction will sooner or later bite someone. But I agree that unnecessary nesting of the same kind of quote is poor style and should be discouraged.; f"Please, have some {assorted_snacks['for_guests'].serve()}, they're delicious!"
13. Prevent f-strings from looking like regular Python strings [rejected] - IMO f-strings should continue to look like regular Python strings to a Python programmer and not allow non-intuitive quoting just because the parser can handle this...; I don't think that nesting f-strings should be allowed, but I guess that ship has already sailed.
14. Allow reusing opening quotes inside f-string interpolations [accepted] - It makes it possible to copy any valid expression from another part of the code into an interpolation without having to worry about string quotes.; This increased freedom would be helpful for ad hoc testing/experimenting and avoiding SyntaxError when absent-mindedly reusing opening quotes in a REPL session.
15. Keep restriction on reusing same quote character to prevent arbitrary nesting [rejected] - Nested f-strings like f"{f"infinite"}" are incredibly difficult for a human to parse IMHO and require tools to be aligned about how to help the user understand them.; By keeping the quote restriction, arbitrary nesting can be prevented while still simplifying implementation and removing annoying bits like backslash limitations.
16. Formalize tokenizer tokens FSTRING_START, FSTRING_MIDDLE, FSTRING_END in grammar [accepted] - The tokens in the PEP are there just for reference to understand what they do but they are an implementation detail and not a public API definition.; The tokenizer module in the reference implementation seems to have not caught up with the PEP yet because it is Python and not the private C implementation.
17. Support arbitrary nesting of f-strings by removing string literal quoting rules [rejected] - Harder for beginners to parse at a glance. This feature absolutely requires some kind of syntax highlighting / code-formatting to understand what is happening in the code. This is a drastic increase in complexity.; I think we need to be careful relying on syntax highlighting as a cure for confusing syntax and what about visually impaired programmers or other folks for which highlighting might not help or be available?
18. Allow f-strings to contain full Python expressions including statements [rejected] - Most of the time there's just no reason to put anything beyond a mere variable name or a very simple expression and beginners aren't expected to know the full grammar of the language.; This is already possible in 3.10, but I strongly doubt that it was ever intended and should we really head on in the same direction even more?
19. Allow reusing the same quote style inside f-strings [rejected] - Personally, I found the prohibition on reusing the same quote mildly annoying.
20. Restrict f-string tokenization details in the PEP [rejected] - What these tokens (the ones in the C tokenizer, which I insist is not visible) will contain is going to be based fundamentally on what makes the implementation simpler.
21. Allow infinite nesting with quote switching restrictions [rejected] - Preventing nesting entirely wouldn't be backwards compatible, f-strings can already be nested if you use different quote styles for each level.
22. Rename FSTRING_END to cover only the closing quote [rejected] - In general, you should not focus on what the tokens contain.
23. Move quote reuse restrictions from grammar to linters [rejected] - Ultimately(in my opinion), such restrictions belong in linters and code formatters rather than in the language grammar itself.
24. Symmetric token contents including quotes [rejected] - I apologize if it seems that I am overly insisting on this, but I think is important because the proposal doesn't change any user-visible thing if the tokens contain the starting quote or not
25. Allow backslash escapes for curly braces instead of doubling [rejected] - I believe that when PEP 498 was discussed, there was a good reason to use the latter, but somehow I can't find that reason in the PEP; In any case, I think the question is if we can support both, right (for backwards compat). The double { makes it somehow harder to implement
26. Allow newlines inside format specifiers without backslash continuation [accepted] - Both of these are valid with our current implementation: f"___{ x }___" and f"___{( x )}___"; It also handles debug expressions: f"___{ 1 + 1 =}___" which prints the formatted result with newlines preserved.
27. Use parser-driven mode switching instead of modifying the tokenizer [accepted] - That could be driven by the parser though, right? The parser can have lookaheads for }, : and :=, and then signal to the lexer to switch back.; In general, we found that just modifying the tokenizer to know when to switch is not only much easier, but also much cleaner and debuggable
28. Add PEP 8 guidance discouraging reliance on quote reuse in f-strings [open] - I would also like to see the PEP more strongly discourage actually relying on that in manually written code, in the form of a proposed addition to PEP 8.; The section on string quotes would be the appropriate place for an addition like: (The part in parentheses probably shouldn't be added to PEP 8)
29. Provide a regular expression specification for f-string token types [rejected] - I think it would help if there was a specification for the tokens – not for what is returned by the tokenizer, but e.g. a regular expression showing what the lexer accepts for each token.; I don't think a regular expression is possible (or at least straightforward so it helps for clarifications) because the cut points depend on the level of parenthesis
30. Using backslash escapes instead of doubled braces [rejected] - The doubling has always irked me, and I think I've forgotten that it existed several times over the years; In any case, I think the question is if we can support both, right (for backwards compat). The double { makes it somehow harder to implement but I don't think there is a way around supporting it
31. Allowing newlines inside f-string expressions [accepted] - It's unclear from the PEP whether following (new line in f-expression) are valid or not; But I can confirm that this will be incorporated soon into the PEP document
32. Clarifying tokenizer behavior after colon in format specifiers [accepted] - Step 3 doesn't say anything special about what happens after a : character is encountered; I think we may want to be a bit more explicit here, but the section was intended to be indicative and not prescriptive as different tokenizers would require different ways to approach the problem
33. Supporting quote reuse inside f-string expressions [accepted] - Personally, I don't find any of the arguments against supporting quote reuse to be compelling; Not sure this is worth debating any more… the PEP was accepted into Python 3.12
34. Increasing the limit for nested format specifiers [rejected] - Another small topic that isn't mentioned in the PEP has to do with nested format specifiers. It appears that the implementation supports two levels of nesting but not three; For both of these things we just preserved existing behavior, while for the nesting of f-strings we had to dictate it because now arbitrary nesting is possible while before it was not

Group the numbers that describe the SAME idea. Every number must appear in exactly one group; an idea
with no duplicate is a group of one. Give each group the clearest, most specific title.

Restrict or allow arbitrary nesting of quotes/braces in f-strings
Allow and document quote reuse inside f-string expressions
Require parentheses around expressions containing same-quote nesting
Document IDLE limitations and PEP 8 guidance regarding quote reuse in f-strings
Allow single quotes inside double-quoted f-string expressions
Tokenization details, token names, and preventing f-strings from looking like regular strings
Prevent arbitrary nesting of f-strings to maintain readability without relying on syntax highlighting
Allow f-strings to contain full Python statements (rejected)
Move quote reuse restrictions from grammar to linters
Allow newlines inside f-string expressions and format specifiers
Use parser-driven mode switching instead of modifying the tokenizer
Clarify tokenizer behavior after colon in format specifiers
Increase limit for nested format specifiers (rejected)
